# #4682: Patch: the clock alarm covers the mulligan and background tabs
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

You queue, get paired, and switch tabs; today nothing calls you back with sound. Your turn and prompt alarms stay silent in a hidden tab, and the 45-second mulligan countdown never sounds at all. Miss your prompt and the server lets the AI policy answer for you; miss the mulligan and you keep your whole hand unpicked. After this, your own turn, prompt and mulligan countdowns beat in their last seconds whether or not the tab is visible.

## Why

`apps/web/src/game/Clock.tsx` wires the alarm only for `kind === "turn"` and `kind === "prompt"`, and its comment says the mulligan (`side null`) stays silent. `apps/web/src/audio/engine.ts` (`accepting()`) returns false while the page is hidden, so every `playSfx`, including the alarm beats `stepClockAlarm` schedules, is dropped in a hidden tab; the 200ms repaint that schedules them is throttled there too. SPEC R79: on prompt-clock expiry the server answers with the AI policy. SPEC R268: the two mulligans share one 45s clock a player's answer neither stops nor extends. PR #4528 deliberately quieted background tabs (crowd, SFX, voices); PR #4573 added the own-prompt alarm afterwards, so the conflict is new and the alarm's whole job is catching a player who looked away.

## Proposal

Include the viewer's mulligan countdown in the alarm schedule with the same beats. Exempt only the alarm beats (`heartbeat`/`clockTick` from `audio/clockAlarm.ts`) from the hidden-tab gate so a hidden tab still sounds your own clocks, keeping everything else silent. Schedule defensively for throttled repaint: plan beats from the server frame and skip late ones per `CLOCK_ALARM_LATE_MS` as today.

## Where it lands

`apps/web/src/game/Clock.tsx`, `apps/web/src/audio/useTurnClockAlarm.ts`, `apps/web/src/audio/clockAlarm.ts`, `apps/web/src/audio/engine.ts` (plus `constants.ts`), and the tests beside each (`clockAlarm.test.ts`, `engine.test.ts`, `Clock.test.tsx` patterns). No engine or spec rule changes: this presents the existing clocks (SPEC §2.1, §9.5, §10.11).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The viewer's foreground mulligan countdown beats in its last seconds; the opponent's side stays silent.
- [ ] In a hidden tab the viewer's own turn clock and prompt countdown still beat; crowd, effects and voices stay silent.
- [ ] Muted, pre-gesture, or context-less states stay silent exactly as today.
- [ ] Late beats are skipped, never stacked, on return to the tab.
- [ ] The touched vitest files pass (`pnpm --dir apps/web test <file>`); no new lint suppressions.

## Size and risks

Medium: one audio-engine carve-out plus schedule tests. Risk: browsers may suspend a background AudioContext (the engine already tears down closed ones); the tab-title "Your turn" (#1792) remains the fallback. Rejected alternative: desktop notifications (needs permission prompts) and reusing music's `playMusicInBackground` (wrong channel for an alarm).
